text:
jamie: Quick dump from the new load rig. Ran replay harness vs synthetic across kernel-selector v2 + speculative decoding on quantized 4-bit kernels. TL;DR: replay warmup helps p50 but we see a p95 tail regression when speculative is enabled on q4_fastrun.

alex: Can you paste the exact command and the top-line numbers? Was KV cache primed the same way for both runs?

jamie: Command and short results below. KV priming: same trace, same prefix length 512 tokens. No sampling, deterministic seed.

jamie: ```
./bench/run_load 
  --mode replay 
  --trace=prod_trace_2026-03-10.json 
  --kernel_policy=auto:v2 
  --kv_warmup=prefix:512 
  --speculative=on 
  --quant=q4_fastrun 
  --seed=42
```

jamie: Summary numbers (mean of 5 runs):
- replay + spec + q4_fastrun: p50=17.1ms, p95=128ms, throughput=980 req/s
- synthetic + spec + q4_fastrun: p50=18.3ms, p95=112ms, throughput=970 req/s
- replay + no-spec + q4_fastrun: p50=17.0ms, p95=110ms, throughput=985 req/s

maria: Interesting — p50 is slightly better with replay, but p95 regresses only when speculative is on and using q4_fastrun. That implies speculative path + quantized kernel interaction.

kevin: :thinking: Does the kernel selector switch to a fallback kernel mid-request? Any logs showing kernel change on high-latency samples?

jamie: Saw a few fallbacks in the logs. Example: `kernel selected: q4_fastrun` then later `kernel fallback: fp16_generic` with a 30ms switch. Snip: 

jamie: ```
[13:12:11.345] request_id=abc kernel_selected=q4_fastrun seq=0
[13:12:11.378] request_id=abc speculative_emit=true token=...
[13:12:11.410] request_id=abc kernel_fallback=fp16_generic reason=kv_miss_latency
```

sara: That fallback would explain p95 spikes. If speculative tries to emit while kv cache lookup isn't ready on q4_fastrun path, we hit the slow fallback. Did you profile KV lookup distribution?

jamie: Yes — kv lookup tail is worse under replay because replay includes more long-prefix hits that exercise larger KV pages. Median kv_lookup=0.9ms, p99 kv_lookup=45ms under replay; synthetic has p99 ~18ms.

bench-bot: Perf note: batching window shrank from 3.2ms -> 1.1ms when speculative enabled (observed on q4_fastrun). Likely due to early emits preventing batching coalescing.

alex: So two interacting effects: (1) replay warmup increases cache pressure/p99 kv latency, (2) speculative causes early emits which reduce effective batching, (3) quantized kernel has different memory access pattern causing higher fallback probability.

maria: For apples-to-apples we should run: identical trace, fixed random seed, identical concurrency, and record kernel-switch counts, batch sizes, and kv latencies per-request. Also add a run with `speculative=probe` (emit-only-if-cache-ready) vs `speculative=always` to isolate behavior.

kevin: Agreed. Also add `--batch_coalesce_timeout=3ms` vs `1ms` sweep. If coalescing is the culprit, increasing window should recover p95.

jamie: I'll add those sweeps. Preliminary local probe: setting coalesce to 4ms drops p95 from 128ms -> 116ms for replay+spec+q4_fastrun, and reduces kernel fallbacks by ~60%.

sara: Good. Also run with `--quant=q8_dynamic` to see if higher-bit quant avoids fallback. Might trade cost for tail.

jamie: Ran q8_dynamic quick check: p50 ~18.0ms, p95 ~114ms (replay+spec). So slightly worse p50 but much closer p95.

maria: This suggests a quality/perf tradeoff — q4 gives better median but brittle tails with speculative. We should encode this into the regression gate: any perf job that enables speculative must check kernel_fallback_rate and kv_p99 delta. If fallback_rate > 2% or kv_p99 increases > 10% trigger fail.

prod-bot: regression-gate: scan completed. Candidate: kernel-selector-v2 + speculative default on for q4 profile. Result: tail_latency_increase=14% (FAIL) -> blocking rollout.

kevin: Sounds right. Action items: (1) jamie: run full apples-to-apples sweep (seeded, batch timeout sweep, speculative modes, q4/q8) and dump `per-request` CSV with columns [req_id, kernel_seq, fallback_flag, batch_size, kv_lookup_ms, emit_time_ms]. (2) sara: update kernel selector to prefer fp16 fallback earlier? Maybe a cost heuristic to avoid expensive fallback mid-request. (3) infra: consider KV page pressure mitigations for replay rigs.

jamie: I'll run the sweep tonight and push results to the bench board. Will include a small harness change to log `kernel_switch_count` per-request.

alex: Thanks. If you can include a short repro that reliably triggers fallback we can add it to the regression tests (so future kernel selector or speculative changes don't regress silently).

jamie: Will do. Adding test plan to the PR: add synthetic trace that mirrors replay prefix distribution + enable speculative=always + q4_fastrun. Repro threshold: >1% fallback rate over 10k requests.

maria: Perfect. Once we have the sweep artifacts we can decide whether to: 1) disable speculative for q4 in default config, 2) bump quant to q8 for speculative path, or 3) tune batching/coalesce to recover tail.

sara: Minor: log line formatting for fallback currently drops stack; please include `selector_state` in logs so we know why fallback happened (kv_miss vs kernel_exception).

jamie: Noted. I'll include selector_state and increase log sampling to 0.5% for tail debugging.

prod-bot: deploy note: rollback candidate flagged for canary. Hold any speculative-default rollouts for q4 until bench sweep is confirmed.

alex: Thanks everyone. Short-term: jamie runs sweep, we add regression test. Mid-term: think about kernel/kv co-design to avoid these brittle interactions. :thumbsup:
